description: An API registered by walking a registry. One call site, many addresses: `for (const endpoint of endpoints) fastify.all('/' + endpoint.name, handler)` over a module that re-exports 438 endpoints was enumerated as TWO anonymous rows at `<unresolved:endpoint.name>`, which is a rounding error rather than a surface. The collection is knowable here -- `Object.entries` over a namespace import is a set of names the compiler already holds, carried across a `.map` that keeps the key as `name` -- so the path is folded once per element. Three properties are asserted together. The registry expands to one row per endpoint and NOT two: the loop registers in both branches of a condition, and an address exists once however many implementations sit behind it. The `register(plugin, { prefix })` mount is applied to routes the plugin's own file never states, because a route recorded without its prefix names an address that answers nothing. And the negative is the point of the whole thing: a loop over a collection assembled at runtime keeps its single unresolved row, because 438 phantom addresses would do far more damage than one honest `<unresolved>`.
